Air Peace says all is set to open a new international travel corridor between the United Kingdom and South-East Nigeria with the commencement of its London-Owerri flight operations effective 15 December. The airline, in a statement on Monday, said the new service is expected to bring considerable relief to residents of Imo State and neighbouring states, particularly families, businesspeople and members of the Nigerian diaspora who have had to contend with the inconvenience of travelling through other airports before connecting to their destinations in the South-East. The airline said the new connection would operate from London’s Gatwick and Heathrow airports, giving travellers greater flexibility when planning their journeys. Air Peace attributed the development to a joint effort by the Imo State and Federal Governments, particularly the contributions of Governor Hope Uzodimma and the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo. The airline noted that the minister played a key role in securing President Bola Tinubu’s approval for Owerri Airport to commence international operations. NIN for domestic flights sparks privacy, access concerns Delta killings: Obi demands justice for four NDC supporters ‘Rig and die’ rhetoric fuelling Delta tension – Keyamo The airline added that beyond passenger convenience, “the new route is expected to provide opportunities for stronger family connections, business exchanges and tourism between the United Kingdom and South-Eastern Nigeria.” The carrier explained that passengers will be flown aboard Air Peace’s premium Boeing 777 wide-body aircraft, “which offers spacious cabins, comfortable seating and inflight meals featuring Nigerian and international cuisine.” The airline also highlighted its baggage allowances as part of the benefits of the service. Economy Class passengers will be entitled to two checked bags weighing 23 kg each, while Business Class travellers will enjoy two bags weighing 32 kg each. Air Peace said the new connection was part of its broader ambition to expand its international and domestic operations while making air travel more accessible to Nigerians.
